provenance.keySource: A question is authenticated when its printed NTA question id is in the 24-05-2026 (Second) final key for subject 322 and the key option id is one of its four printed option ids. Facts written first: tmp/1123-papers/physics/checkA/A_facts_before_search.txt. Search: tmp/1123-papers/physics/checkA/s.mjs over the served copy and the deck, plus a full list of served stems (stems.txt); builder build_A.mjs checks every cited id.
eliminationNote: Q16 is called covered partly by elimination: served material makes A and B false and D true, which leaves option 3 (C and D); C itself is taught only as "an ammeter needs a small, a voltmeter a large resistance", not as the ideal zero/infinite. Q2 D and Q21 rest on short inferences from the stated card (Gauss law is based on the inverse square law; the same flux links all N turns). Checker B should rule on Q2, Q16 and Q21 first. Q7 is NOT covered only because its one matching row (118066da) has a retracted wrong line in its working: repairing that explanation would make Q7 covered.
paperStructure: One compulsory Physics section of 50 stand-alone MCQs (Q391-440), no comprehension passage; 24-05-2026 Second shift; NTA final key has 50 rows, none dropped.

facts: In a uniform field the forces +qE and -qE on a dipole cancel: net force zero (only a torque)

matches.teaches: net force on a dipole in a uniform field is zero; it feels a torque
in a uniform field a dipole has torque p x E but no net force

questions.reason: Key card asks the same thing: the net force on a dipole in a uniform field is zero.

facts: A false: charge is quantised, q = ne, not any value
B: Gauss law holds for any closed surface and any charge distribution
C: a charge outside a closed surface gives zero net flux
D: Gauss law rests on the inverse-square dependence, so holds for any inverse-square field

matches.teaches: charge is always an integral multiple of e
Gauss law is true for any closed surface, whatever its shape or size
total flux is zero if no charge is enclosed
q in Gauss law is only the charge inside S
Gauss law is based on the inverse square dependence of Coulomb law
flux through a closed surface enclosing no net charge is zero: lines that enter leave

questions.reason: Cards make charge quantised (A false), Gauss law true for any closed surface, flux zero with no charge enclosed (only enclosed charge counts) and Gauss law based on the inverse square law, so B, C and D.

facts: Infinite plane sheet: E = sigma/2 eps0, independent of r
infinite line charge: E proportional to 1/r
point charge: 1/r^2
short dipole: 1/r^3

matches.teaches: infinite plane sheet E = sigma/2 eps0 (no r)
infinite line charge E = lambda/(2 pi eps0 r)
dipole field 1/r^3 against 1/r^2 for a point charge

questions.reason: Cards give the sheet field without r, the line-charge field as 1/r and contrast the dipole 1/r^3 with the point charge 1/r^2: all four pairs.

facts: Force on the end charge Q: kQQ/(2a)^2 + kqQ/a^2 = 0, so q = -Q/4
questions.reason: No served bank row solves for the charge that keeps a three-charge line in equilibrium (Coulomb force balance on an end charge); cards give Coulomb law only, which cannot cover a numerical.

facts: Every element of the ring is at distance R from the centre: V = kQ/R = 1.8e7 V

matches.teaches: potential at the centre of a uniformly charged ring = kQ/a, worked with numbers

questions.reason: Served bank row asks the potential at the centre of a charged ring with V = kQ/R, the same formula and steps with other numbers.

facts: Three equal C in series: C/3; in parallel: 3C; ratio C1/C2 = 1/9
questions.reason: Bank rows combine two unequal capacitors in series for a voltage or an energy, and one states only that parallel raises and series lowers capacitance; none works out series and parallel values of equal capacitors and their ratio.

facts: q = CV kept when joined to an equal uncharged capacitor
common potential V/2
energy = 1/2 (2C)(V/2)^2 = 2e-6 J, half the initial
questions.reason: The one served row with the same steps (118066da, a charged capacitor shared with an equal uncharged one, energy halves) has a working that first writes a wrong line (2C*V0^2/4 = CV0^2/2) and then retracts it with "oh wait check"; a bank item with a wrong working does not count, so not covered. The row should be repaired.

facts: emf = work / charge
electric field = force / charge
current density = current / area
mobility = drift velocity / electric field

matches.teaches: emf is the work done per unit charge by the source
field = force on a test charge divided by the charge
current per unit area I/A is current density
mobility = drift velocity per unit electric field
matches conductivity, mobility, resistivity and drift velocity expressions

questions.reason: Four cards give the four definitions in the match.

facts: Resistivity: copper (1.7e-8) < iron (~1e-7) < carbon graphite (~3.5e-5) < rubber (1e13-1e16 ohm m)
so conductivity ascending: rubber, carbon, iron, copper
questions.reason: Cards rank conductors, semiconductors and insulators and give the resistivity ranges of metals and semiconductors, but nothing served gives the resistivities of copper, iron, carbon and rubber (NCERT Table 3.1), so copper above iron and carbon between iron and rubber is not taught.

facts: A false: a current-carrying wire is electrically neutral
B true: higher temperature, more collisions, smaller tau, smaller drift velocity
C false: emf does not depend on internal resistance
D true: dry cells have much higher internal resistance than common electrolytic cells
questions.reason: Cards teach D (dry cells have much higher internal resistance) and B (more frequent collisions with temperature, vd = eE tau/m), but nothing served says a current-carrying wire is electrically neutral (A), which separates the key (B, D) from option A, B, D; nor that emf is independent of internal resistance.

facts: R_T = R_0 [1 + alpha (T - T0)]
questions.reason: Cards give rho_T = rho_0 [1 + alpha (T - T0)], but no served bank row solves a temperature-coefficient numerical (find the temperature for a given rise in resistance).

facts: Balance P/Q = R/S; after swapping P and Q: Q/P = R'/S
multiply: S^2 = R R', S = sqrt(500 x 505) = 502.5 ohm
questions.reason: The only bridge row is a metre-bridge balance for one unknown (22940911); no served row uses the interchange of P and Q and S = sqrt(R R'), a different set of steps.

facts: F = q v x B: v parallel to B gives zero force

matches.teaches: positive charge moving parallel to a uniform B: force zero (sin 0 = 0)

questions.reason: Served bank row asks the same thing with the same answer.

facts: A ferromagnetic (soft iron) core makes the field inside a solenoid larger

matches.teaches: a large field is possible by inserting a soft iron core inside the solenoid
ferromagnetic substances are strongly magnetised in an external field
a soft iron core in a solenoid increases the flux for a given current

questions.reason: Card says a soft-iron core gives a large field inside the solenoid, and a bank row says the core increases the flux; soft iron is the ferromagnetic case.

facts: Orbiting electron: current I = e nu (charge per revolution x frequency)
m = I A = e nu pi r^2

matches.teaches: orbiting electron: I = e/T, m = I x pi r^2 = evr/2, with numbers

questions.reason: Served bank row finds the orbital magnetic moment of an electron by I = e/T and m = I pi r^2, the same formula and steps (it starts from the speed instead of the frequency).

facts: A false: torque on a planar loop depends on its area, not its shape
B false: antiparallel currents repel
C true: ideal ammeter zero resistance, ideal voltmeter infinite
D true: galvanometer -> voltmeter with a high resistance in series

matches.teaches: torque NIAB sin theta depends only on the area of the loop, not its shape
parallel currents attract, antiparallel currents repel
ammeter: small shunt in parallel; voltmeter: large resistance in series
ammeter effect negligible when its resistance is small
large resistance in series makes a voltmeter that draws very little current

questions.reason: A bank row says torque depends only on the area, a card makes antiparallel currents repel, and cards give the voltmeter conversion and why an ammeter must have small and a voltmeter large resistance; with A and B false, C and D is the only option left. C is taught only as small/large resistance, not as the ideal zero/infinite.

facts: I = B/(mu0 n) = 2.0 A
questions.reason: Cards and a bank row give B = mu0 n I as an expression (ea2c1bf1 asks which expression gives B), but no served bank row solves a solenoid numerical for the current.

facts: Torque on the magnet m B sin(theta) = 3 x 0.25 x 0.5 = 0.375 N m
balanced by F x 0.1 m, F = 3.75 N
questions.reason: No served bank row balances the torque m B sin(theta) on a bar magnet against an applied force; the nearest rows find work in rotating a dipole or the torque on a loop.

facts: Straight leads along radii give no field at O
three-quarter arc: B = (3/4) mu0 I / 2R = 1.57e-4 T
questions.reason: Bank rows give the field at the centre of a full loop (B = mu0 I/2R), but none takes a fraction of a loop or uses radial leads that add nothing; different steps.

facts: Mutual inductance depends on the coils' geometry, separation and relative orientation, not on the currents

matches.teaches: mutual inductance depends on separation and relative orientation
mutual inductance depends on the geometry and relative orientation of the coils

questions.reason: Key card and a bank row state the fact the key rests on.

facts: The same flux links every turn: flux linkage N Phi is proportional to N, so tripling the turns triples it

matches.teaches: for a closely wound coil of N turns the same flux is linked with all the turns
flux linkage through a coil of N turns is N Phi

questions.reason: Cards define the flux linked with a coil as N Phi with the same flux through every turn, so it triples with the turns.

facts: Steady d.c. (omega = 0): an inductor conducts (X_L = omega L = 0), a capacitor blocks after charging
an inductor does not have infinite resistance in d.c.
questions.reason: Cards say current stops once a capacitor is charged on d.c. and that X_L is proportional to frequency, but nothing served says an inductor passes steady d.c. or has no infinite resistance in d.c.; reaching it needs the unstated step that d.c. means zero frequency.

facts: In a pure inductor the current lags the voltage by pi/2

matches.teaches: in a purely inductive circuit the current lags the voltage by 90 degrees

questions.reason: Served bank row states the same fact.

facts: X_L = 2 pi f L = 78.5 ohm
I_rms = V_rms / X_L = 2.8 A
questions.reason: Bank rows compute a capacitive reactance (2be3fcb0), an inductive reactance from an impedance (03e23eee) and an inductor voltage from given reactances (d01eb790), but none computes X_L = 2 pi f L and then I = V/X_L.

facts: e = N A dB/dt with A = pi (0.01)^2 and dB/dt = 5000/4
N = e / (A dB/dt) = 28
questions.reason: Bank rows compute the induced emf from N, A and the field change (e6aaca54, 0eaa849e); none solves Faraday's law for the number of turns, a different unknown.

facts: Photon energy E = h nu rises with frequency
frequency order: microwaves < infrared < ultraviolet < X-rays

matches.teaches: gamma, X-rays, UV, visible, infrared, microwaves, radio in increasing wavelength
photon energy E = h nu = hc/lambda
explanation lists radio, microwaves, infrared, visible, UV, X-rays, gamma by wavelength

questions.reason: Cards order the spectrum by wavelength and make photon energy hc/lambda, so energy rises from microwaves to X-rays.

facts: Conduction current in the wires equals the displacement current in the capacitor gap (current continuity, Ampere-Maxwell)
NTA key: the source may be a.c. or d.c.
questions.reason: Cards define displacement current and total current = conduction + displacement, and one says displacement current may be zero for steady fields; nothing served states that conduction current equals displacement current for an a.c. or a d.c. source.

facts: A: all em waves travel at the same speed in vacuum
B: a fully charged capacitor has no changing field, so no displacement current
C false: infrared, not ultraviolet, is used to see through haze and fog
D false: an accelerated (circling) charge radiates em waves
questions.reason: Cards give A (same speed in vacuum), B (displacement current from a time-varying field; current stops once a capacitor is charged) and D (accelerated charges radiate), but nothing served says which radiation sees through haze and fog, and C is what separates the key (A, B) from A, B, C.

facts: Momentum delivered by radiation of energy U: U/c if absorbed, 2U/c if perfectly reflected
questions.reason: Cards give a photon momentum p = h nu/c, but nothing served states the momentum delivered to a surface by radiation, or that perfect reflection doubles it to 2U/c.

facts: Intensity I = (1/2) c eps0 E0^2, so E0 ~ 4.3e8 V/m
questions.reason: A bank row finds E0 from the intensity (f4fd675c) and another relates E0 = c B0 the other way round (011459c4), but no single served row goes from intensity to the magnetic amplitude; the two steps are split across rows.

facts: Covering half a lens still gives the whole image, with reduced intensity
questions.reason: The one card on this is about a concave mirror with half its surface covered (whole image, lower intensity); nothing served states it for a lens. The principle transfers, but the stated fact is for a mirror, so doubtful.

facts: Refractive indices: CO2 (~1.00045) < water (1.33) < crown glass (1.52) < diamond (2.42)
questions.reason: No served card or row gives the refractive indices of carbon dioxide, water, crown glass and diamond (NCERT Table 9.1).

facts: Wider slit: more light, brighter maxima
one slit closed: interference disappears
wider source slit: pattern less sharp
lower frequency (longer lambda): fringe width lambda D/d increases
questions.reason: Cards give the fringe positions x = n lambda D/d (so fringe width grows with wavelength) and the single-slit pattern, but nothing served says that widening the source slit blurs the fringes or that widening one slit raises the maximum intensity.

facts: Two slits at the centre: 4 I0 = I
one slit closed: I0 = I/4
questions.reason: A served row uses I = 4 I0 cos^2(phi/2) and notes the maximum 4 I0 at zero path difference (75299146), but it finds the two-source intensity from I0, the reverse unknown; doubtful, so not covered.

facts: Frequency unchanged in the liquid: v = nu lambda = 2.25e8 m/s
questions.reason: A card says the frequency does not change on refraction, but no served bank row finds a refractive index from the frequency and the wavelength in a medium (v = nu lambda, n = c/v).

facts: Intensity proportional to slit width: I1/I2 = 4
amplitude ratio 2:1
questions.reason: A served row finds Imax/Imin = 9:1 from an intensity ratio 4:1 (0e2ae512), but the first step here, intensity proportional to slit width, is not taught by any served material, so the steps are not the same.

facts: Mirror magnification m = f/(f - u); u1 = -9 cm, u2 = -15 cm
questions.reason: No served bank row finds a mirror's focal length from the change in magnification when the object is moved; the mirror rows are qualitative.

facts: Threshold wavelength lambda0 = hc/phi0: larger work function, shorter threshold wavelength
order by decreasing lambda0 = increasing phi: Cs, K, Na, Ca

matches.teaches: threshold wavelength = hc/phi
greater work function, higher threshold frequency

questions.reason: Bank explanation gives the threshold wavelength as hc/phi and a card says a greater work function needs a higher threshold frequency, so the order follows from the given work functions.

facts: de Broglie p = h/lambda for the electron; photon p = h/lambda
same wavelength, same momentum: 1:1

matches.teaches: photon momentum p = h nu/c = h/lambda
de Broglie wavelength lambda = h/p for a particle

questions.reason: A card gives the photon momentum h/lambda and a bank row the de Broglie lambda = h/p, so equal wavelengths mean equal momenta.

facts: Photon energy E = hc/lambda = 3.3e-19 J
photons per second = P / E = 2e20

matches.teaches: lamp 3.3 W at 600 nm: E = hc/lambda, N = P/E

questions.reason: Served bank row is the same sum (600 nm, h = 6.6e-34) with a different power.

facts: Lyman: lower level n1 = 1; Balmer n1 = 2; Paschen n1 = 3; Brackett n1 = 4 in R(1/n1^2 - 1/n2^2)

matches.teaches: match: Lyman n = 1, Balmer n = 2, Paschen n = 3, Brackett n = 4 lower levels
Rydberg formula 1/lambda = R (1/2^2 - 1/3^2) for a Balmer line

questions.reason: Served bank row matches the same four series to their lower levels; another shows the Rydberg form.

facts: Bohr's second postulate: angular momentum is an integral multiple of h/2 pi

matches.teaches: angular momentum is some integral multiple of h/2 pi
angular momentum is nh/2 pi

questions.reason: Key card states the postulate the question asks.

facts: Binding energy per nucleon: 6Li (~5.3 MeV) < 4He (~7.07) < 14N (~7.48) < 12C (~7.68)
questions.reason: Cards give the shape of the binding-energy curve (lower for light nuclei, peak near A = 56) and a bank row gives 7.1 MeV for helium-4, but nothing served gives the values for lithium-6, nitrogen-14 and carbon-12, and the order (He-4 above Li-6, N-14 below C-12) does not follow from the general trend.

matches.teaches: radius for mass number 8A is 2R from R = R0 A^(1/3)

questions.reason: Served bank row uses the same relation for the same mass-number ratio of 8, so the radius ratio is 1:2.

facts: lambda_max = hc / Eg = 1240 eV nm / 0.72 eV ~ 1.7e-6 m
questions.reason: A served row checks whether 450 nm light (2.75 eV) exceeds the silicon gap (0375dea9), but none computes the longest wavelength from the band gap, lambda = hc/Eg.

facts: Forward bias lowers the barrier and narrows the depletion layer

matches.teaches: forward bias narrows the depletion layer
in forward bias the barrier is decreased

questions.reason: Served bank row states that forward bias narrows the depletion layer.

facts: Donor energy level E_D lies slightly below the bottom of the conduction band

matches.teaches: donor level E_D is slightly below the bottom E_C of the conduction band

questions.reason: Key card is the same question and answer.

facts: n_e n_h = n_i^2, so n_h = 1e32 / n_e (1e9; 4e8)
questions.reason: A served row finds n_h = n_i^2 / n_e from a given n_e (fabdd431), but none gets n_e from a doping level in ppm (n_e ~ N_D), the first step of every pair in the match.

facts: Energy per fission 200 MeV = 3.2e-11 J
fissions per second = P / E = 1000 / 3.2e-11 = 3.125e13

matches.teaches: reactor 3.2 MW, 200 MeV per fission: rate = P/E

questions.reason: Served bank row is the same sum with a different power.

facts: At closest approach K = k (2e)(Ze)/d
d = 2kZe^2/K = 4kZe^2/(m v^2), proportional to v^-2

matches.teaches: closest approach: K = (2e)(Ze)/(4 pi eps0 r0), r0 = 2Z e^2/(4 pi eps0 K)
d = 2Ze^2/(4 pi eps0 K)

questions.reason: Served bank row sets the kinetic energy equal to the potential energy at closest approach and finds d inversely proportional to K; with K = mv^2/2 that is v^-2.
